statement: For k=25, if a prime power p^e satisfies p^e >= 25, then in any pairwise-disjoint counterexample family of size 25 (all pairwise gcds <= 24), at most one modulus m_i has v_p(m_i) >= e (else gcd(m_i,m_j) >= p^e >= 25, contradiction).

If index i's p-adic valuation dominates every other modulus's p-adic valuation down to some level c, lowering v_p(m_i) to exactly c changes no pairwise gcd of the family and preserves pairwise disjointness (Lemma 2).

Main reduction theorem: any size-25 counterexample to the disjoint-congruence-classes claim can be transformed (same a_i, same pairwise gcds) into a size-25 counterexample where every modulus divides L = lcm(1,...,24) = 5354228880 = 2^4*3^2*5*7*11*13*17*19*23 (1920 divisors), so a search for a size-25 counterexample may assume WLOG all moduli divide L.

For p in {13,17,19,23} (exactly the primes with k/2 < p < k for k=25) and any size-25 counterexample reduced to divide L, if p divides two distinct moduli m_i,m_j then gcd(m_i,m_j)=p exactly, so the map i -> (a_i mod p) is injective on the index set divisible by p, giving |{i : p | m_i}| <= p, i.e. sum_{i: p|m_i} 1/gcd(m_i,p) <= 1.

Extend Lemma 3's density/injectivity argument to primes p in (k/3,k/2], e.g. p in {9,11} for k=25 (where gcd could be p or 2p, needing a size-2 case split instead of forcing t=1), to squeeze the reduced search domain further before any exhaustive search is attempted.

Using the Main Reduction Theorem's finite domain (moduli restricted to the 1920 divisors of L=lcm(1..24)) plus Lemma 3's per-prime pruning rules, build an actual exhaustiveness certificate (tools/cert.py) that attempts to decide k=25 by exhaustive search, reporting node counts and either a size-25 counterexample or a proof none exists with these moduli.

Check whether the same valuation-lowering technique (Lemma 2) plus Lemma 1's one-exceeder argument generalizes cleanly to arbitrary k (not just k=25), giving a uniform reduction to moduli dividing lcm(1,...,k-1) for every k, as a reusable lemma for future c6(a) attempts at k=26,27,...
